prompt: Which ion does magnesium form, and why?
markscheme: **C.** Mg ($[\text{Ne}]3s^{2}$) loses its two valence electrons to reach the stable configuration of neon, forming Mg²⁺.

prompt: Deduce the formulas of **(a)** aluminium oxide and **(b)** magnesium nitride, and define an ionic bond.
markscheme:
**(a)** Al₂O₃ **(b)** Mg₃N₂ (charges balance: Al³⁺/O²⁻, Mg²⁺/N³⁻) **(A1)**

Ionic bond: electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions **(A1)**

prompt:
**(a)** Explain why solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but molten sodium chloride does. **[2]**

**(b)** Explain why magnesium oxide has a much higher melting point than sodium chloride. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** In the solid lattice the ions are held in fixed positions **(R1)**; when molten the ions are free to move and carry charge **(R1)**

**(b)** Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ have higher charges (and smaller radii) than Na⁺ and Cl⁻, so the electrostatic attractions in the lattice are much stronger **(R1)**
